lane-de-receita.d: A combination of Docker image, checkpoint, overlays and defaults validated together, activated by a wrapper (e.g. start-v030.sh) that exports OVERRIDE_* variables and calls the same start.sh. In the Qwen recipe: day-0, vLLM 0.30, official FP8 and TP1.

imagem-day-0.d: A development image published on a model's launch day (here, vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next, an NVIDIA dev build). It brings support for the model before the stable release, but usually requires patches.

precedencia-de-configuracao.d: The order in which a launcher applies the environment, the .env file, defaults, overrides and guards; the last layer that defines a variable wins. In the Qwen start.sh, the .env beats the command line (except for ABLIT and HF_TOKEN).

variavel-override.d: Variables read by start.sh after the .env (OVERRIDE_MODEL_ID, OVERRIDE_IMAGE, OVERRIDE_KV_CACHE_DTYPE…). They are how the lane wrappers swap the image, checkpoint or defaults without editing the cluster's .env.

hca-gid.d: The HCA (Host Channel Adapter) is the RDMA device NCCL uses (e.g. rocep1s0f0, selected by NCCL_IB_HCA). The GID index picks the entry in the RoCE address table (3 is usually RoCE v2/IPv4; some clusters use 5).

nfs-pseudoroot.d: In NFSv4 the server exposes a virtual tree; the export marked with fsid=0 becomes the root of that tree. The recipe exports the head's Hugging Face cache this way, read-only, for the worker to mount as a Docker volume.

kernel-de-emulacao.d: A fallback path in which quantized weights are dequantized to BF16 (once, at load time) and multiplied by a regular GEMM. Correct, but without the byte savings of the native kernel; used when the matrix shape falls outside the kernel's envelope.

overlay-bind-mount.d: Replacing a package file inside the container by mounting a patched version from the host on top of it (docker -v host:container:ro). It avoids rebuilding the image; it must be done identically on both nodes.

worker-headless.d: A vLLM process on a secondary node that takes part in the distributed model (rank > 0) without starting the API server (--headless). Only the head (rank 0) serves clients.

escape-hatch.d: A launcher's emergency exit for passing options it doesn't know about without editing the script — in the recipe, EXTRA_VLLM_ARGS, appended last and verbatim to the vllm serve line.

ple-ngram.d: The 51.2 B-parameter table of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next indexed by a hash of the bigrams and trigrams of the local context, injected at the layer with index 1. In the vLLM code it is called PLE; it is looked up by gather, with almost no FLOPs.
